labels.notes: I checked each field of EGF.IsEGFErgodic lam F Phi alpha against main.tex:216-222 (Definition 3.1), C-27's corrected text and C-26's corrected text (DEC-146). (i) The generative flow: F : GenerativeFlow S, a Markov kernel with a finite outflow, matching l.161. (ii) The policy: the field policy is EGF.IsEGFPolicy F.policy (Phi i) alpha, with alpha measurable, alpha^i >= 0 and sum_i alpha^i = 1, hence values in [0,1]^p, and pi(s) = sum_i ofReal(alpha^i(s)) delta_{Phi_i(s)}. This is C-27, carried word for word. Weights may be zero, as printed. Alpha is a parameter rather than an existential; the existential form is immediate. (iii) The ergodicity: the field ergodic is IsGroupErgodic lam (egfGroup Phi), where egfGroup is the closure in Equiv.Perm S of the moves. That is the same group as the group of diffeomorphisms they generate, acting the same way. The generalized setting (any measurable space, any measure, not assumed finite) is a weakening. Nothing the corrected statement says is dropped. (iv) The one extra field, nonsingular (lam.map Phi_i << lam and lam.map Phi_i^{-1} << lam), is an honest abstraction and not an added hypothesis on the paper's objects. Every diffeomorphism of a Riemannian manifold preserves the null sets of the volume in both directions, since its inverse is also a diffeomorphism. So on the paper's objects IsEGFErgodic is exactly the corrected def:egf. This is proved for the cases the paper actually uses: C^n diffeomorphisms (n >= 1) of a finite-dimensional space with Haar measure (nonsingular_of_diffeomorph, isEGFErgodic_diffeomorph_iff), affine maps of the torus (nonsingular_torusAffineME) and rotations of the sphere (nonsingular_rotME). The general Riemannian fact cannot be stated at the pin: Mathlib has no manifold volume. I grepped Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian and found only Basic and PathELength. The SCOPE discloses this. It follows the precedent of theo:backward_policy, which is marked on any measurable space with nonsingular moves, and C-6 (applied in v2) already makes the paper state that its moves are nonsingular. (v) I checked FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall by hand. Take the rotation of Fin 4 and lam = delta_0 + delta_2. The element rot^2 swaps the two atoms, so the group is ergodic. The set {0,1} is a.e.-invariant under rot (look at the points 0 and 2), with measure 1 and co-measure 1. And lam{1} = 0 while (rot_* lam){1} = lam{0} = 1. So without nonsingularity the group form does not give C-26's generator form. (vi) The closer's question, the generator form without the field (design B), is a presentation choice that DEC-146 settles, not a reading between two statements of the paper. On the paper's objects B and the chosen design A are the same predicate. DEC-146's parenthetical names both wordings: 'every set a.e.-invariant under all Phi_i is null or conull' and EGF.IsGroupErgodic. A is the only design that satisfies both literally: A = B with the field = (group form) with the field, by isEGFErgodic_iff and isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff. The target block also prescribed A field by field. B differs from A only on singular moves, outside the paper's setting. I confirmed with a probe, now deleted, that B is strictly weaker: the swap of Bool with lam = delta_false satisfies the generator form and its move is singular. So no OQ is needed and the mark does not wait. (vii) isEGFErgodic_iff_symmDiff states C-26's 'that is' word for word, with lam(Set.univ \ A) for lambda(S minus A). With pp.notation false the elaborated statement reads lam (symmDiff (Set.preimage (Phi i) A) A) = 0, so the parse pitfall is avoided. This is the only use of the symmDiff symbol in the code; the others are in docstrings. The mark stands.

In order the docstring has: the title; **`def:egf`** with main.tex:216 at character 230 (within 4000); the paper's l.216-222 quoted as printed; C-27 and C-26's corrected texts quoted as registered; the Hypothesis checklist; the SCOPE (disclosed); the provenance line at character 5410 (within the 8000 of kb 0015). The checklist and SCOPE are true. The checklist marks the space and the moves as weakened, correctly. The SCOPE states truthfully which nonsingularity instances are formalized, which hypotheses are for the universality links only, and the limits of both witnesses (a non-volume lambda, and delta_true not of full support).

corrections.C-26: The proposed anchors prove the corrected form. EGF.IsEGFErgodic is DEC-146's definition. EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_symmDiff equates it with the corrected text word for word, plus the nonsingularity that 'diffeomorphisms' supplies. EGF.isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_iff shows that the generator wording and the group wording agree. EGF.IsEGFErgodic.isKernelErgodic, EGF.isEGFErgodic_iff_isUniversalPolicy and EGF.universality_of_isEGFErgodic tie the clause to C-29's universality, with their hypotheses named: positive weights; a finite invariant lamHat with lamHat << lam and lam << lamHat; [IsFiniteMeasure lam]; measure-preserving moves with p > 0 and the uniform kernel; outflows << lam; IsDenseNonnegConeL2. The refutations hold in both directions in the generalized setting, with honest limits. (1) isEGF_not_isEGFErgodic: lam = volume + Measure.sum of 2^{-intEquivNat n} delta_{n.a}. It is finite (instance), of full support, and invariant under +a and -a up to null sets (orbitLam_map_ac with c = a and c = -a). The orbit, which is countable and so measurable, is exactly invariant. It has positive measure (its atom at 0) and co-measure at least vol(S) = T > 0. The conclusion also proves the move nonsingular, so it is the ergodicity clause that fails. (2) isEGFErgodic_not_isEGF: the identity on Bool with delta_true. Every group is ergodic for a Dirac mass. Words fix every point, so {false}, a neighbourhood of false, is never reached from true. Both statements are non-vacuous and say what the REPORT says. The added_hypotheses = [] proposed for adoption is consistent: the corrected text keeps 'diffeomorphisms', and the forward nonsingularity is C-6's, already applied. C-26 is still 'proved' with its old anchors. The master switches the anchors and adopts under DEC-146 at graduation, as the REPORT says.
corrections.C-27: Carried. The field IsEGFErgodic.policy is EGF.IsEGFPolicy: alpha measurable, non-negative, summing to 1. That is C-27's corrected text, and adding EGF.IsEGFErgodic to C-27's anchors is right.
corrections.C-6: Supporting only. IsEGFErgodic.inflowAC passes the field's forward component to InflowAC.of_map_ac. That is correct, and C-6's anchors are unchanged.

checks.universality_link: Each statement is as claimed and every hypothesis is named in the signature. IsEGFErgodic.isUniversalPolicy needs positive weights, a finite invariant lamHat ~ lam and lam finite. isEGFErgodic_iff_isUniversalPolicy needs the policy, nonsingular moves, positive weights and the same lamHat; its converse goes through isKernelErgodic_of_isUniversalPolicy, which needs only lam finite. universality_of_isEGFErgodic and isUniversalFamilyEps_iff_forall_isEGFErgodic: for measure-preserving moves, p > 0, lam finite and a family of uniform-kernel flows with outflows << lam that contains (pi, f lam) for every f in a set D dense in the non-negative cone of L2, the family is eps-universal iff the group is ergodic. In the reverse direction of the second, the family is non-empty by hdense with hD, so it is not vacuous.
checks.instances: None is vacuous. isEGFErgodic_sphere_two_witness quantifies over the parameters of l2SphericalModel, a structure with a nonempty field (its parameter set contains 0). isEGFErgodic_circleRotFlow_iff is a real iff with Mathlib's AddCircle.ergodic_add_left. _sqrt_two and Swap.isEGFErgodic_flow are concrete. The torus and sphere iff theorems go through egfGroup = torusAffineGroup and egfGroup = sphereRotGroup, both by rfl, and the nonsingularity follows from measure preservation.

findings.what: The question meant for the author says the other design, with no 'nonsingular' field and the generator form as the definition, 'is strictly stronger in general'. As a predicate it is strictly weaker than IsEGFErgodic: IsEGFErgodic implies it (via ergodic_moves) and not conversely (the swap of Bool with lam = delta_false satisfies the generator form with a singular move). Only its ergodicity clause is stronger than the group-form clause (isGroupErgodic_egfGroup_of_forall; FourCycle.isGroupErgodic_not_forall). Read the other way, the sentence would tell the author the opposite of the fact.
findings.fix: Reword before anything reaches the author: 'The other design (no nonsingular field, the generator form as the definition) is a strictly weaker predicate in general, since singular moves are admitted, and agrees on the paper's objects.' The question can then be closed as settled by DEC-146: it is a presentation choice and needs no OQ.

notes: Optional follow-up, not a defect: the SCOPE says truthfully that a full-support converse witness is not formalized. In the paper's exact setting one exists. The hyperbolic automorphism catMat = [[2,1],[1,1]] of T^2 with Lebesgue measure is ergodic but fixes 0, so it is a DEC-146 EGF that is topologically ergodic in neither printed reading. Once T-egf-tori-minimal graduates (its file proves noPeriodicVector_catMat and ergodic_torusAffine_of_noPeriodic*), that witness could replace or complement isEGFErgodic_not_isEGF. Also confirmed: kb proposal 2 (in Lean, Phi ⁻¹' A ∆ A, written without parentheses, parses as Phi ⁻¹' (A ∆ A) because ∆ is infixl:100 and ⁻¹' is infixl:80) and kb proposal 4 (inferInstance fails for NoAtoms (volume : Measure (AddCircle T)) at the pin; tested with a probe, now deleted). The Furstenberg (1961) citation for a minimal analytic diffeomorphism of T^2 that is not ergodic for Lebesgue measure is the standard example. It is cited, not claimed as formalized.
